In today's society, many people agree that having a simple goal and achieving it is better than having a huge goal and failing to achieve it, but I disagree. One of the greatest artists, Michelangelo, said that setting our aim too low and achieving it is a great danger for some of us. He stated this thought because he failed and made mistakes before he was known as a great artist. Michelangelo rather fail by doing something big than his life than doing something small and achieving it. I agree with Michelangelo because you learn from past mistakes, you learn to take risks, and having bigger goals help you improve one's self.

Michelangelo is a great artist because of his work, but he learned from his own work to keep moving forward. People can learn from past mistakes by seeing what went wrong and practice doing better at it; for example, in a show called

Master chef, chefs must impress the judges by their skills in cooking, but one chef gets eliminated every episode. When a chef gets eliminated their dreams may get crushed, but they had the courage to go on and did their best and can learn what they did wrong. Another example is taking the permit test as a teenager. The permit test is something big for teens since it is something related to their future. When I took the test I was nervous and failed by one question, but I checked the answers I got wrong and studied them a bit more and passed the next time I took it. These examples prove that you have the ability to learn from past mistakes, grow as a person, and that you might have to take risks in doing so.

Taking risks are mostly involved in big decisions that involve jobs, education, etc. I believe that taking risks are better than small decisions even if those risks don't turn out the way you wanted them too. In a show called Shark Tank, people come in to persuade investors to invest in their products, but they do not always succeed. The people who do not get investments keep moving forward and take their own risks to get an investor. If you learn to take risks, you later get use to it, and you can speak more in front of people and state your opinion. Another example is having a meeting for a job. It is best to have a meeting in person than online because it is not as easy, so you get challenged and the person interviewing can know you better, and you can most likely get the position. Taking risks can make you a better person as a whole and those mistakes can help you improve.

Michelangelo and I agree that having a bigger goal and failing is better than having a small goal and achieving it. Having a bigger goal can increase your confidence and help you put your head in the task you want to overcome. People view their mistakes and overcome it, so they can do better next time. Small goals do not involve much effort and work as bigger achievements; by choosing to accomplish a simple task, you as a person may get use to the easy way out and can get lake over time. Setting a higher aim for yourself is better because you can improve your skills and knowledge. Bigger goals are better because of how much they help you improve.

A great artist once said it is great danger setting a small aim for yourself. Setting a bigger aim and failing is best because you learn from your mistakes, you learn to take risks, and bigger goals help improve one's self. Smaller aims are a scapegoat compared to bigger aims because of how much easier they are. It is best to challenge yourself so that you are ready for anything that comes your way. Oven if you take the high route and fail, it does not mean you can try again. In conclusion, setting a bigger aim and failing is alright and better than setting a small aim due to it being easier.

text: We all have to face the reality of death at some point in our lives, and it can be a very difficult thing to come to terms with. When dealing with the death of a loved one, grief is something that we must learn how to deal with in order for us to move on afterwards. It's not easy, but understanding the various stages of grief can help make this process go more smoothly. The first stage is denial - when we just don't want to accept what has happened; it's too hard and too painful for us so we shut down emotionally and block it out completely. This feeling will eventually pass as time goes by, but it could take weeks or months before you realize that your loved one really isn't coming back again no matter how much you wish they were here still. The second stage is anger - usually an emotion directed towards God (or whoever else) asking why such a terrible thing had happened when life seemed so good beforehand. We may feel like nothing will ever be alright again and lash out angrily towards those around us who are also trying their best to help during this difficult period. But remember that this emotion usually passes over time too – try talking through your emotions if possible instead of bottling them up inside as eventually these feelings should start dissipating soon enough without any long-term harm done. The third stage is bargaining - where we try desperately searching for answers as well as solutions which would somehow bring back our lost loved one from beyond the grave even though deep down inside we know nothing can do so realistically speaking. You'll find yourself making promises or pleading offers hoping against hope that somehow things turn out differently from what you're expecting.but unfortunately there's never going guarantee either way!. . The fourth stage is depression - where sadness sets in about having been robbed off someone close forever; feelings of helplessness overwhelm you because now whatever happens next depends entirely upon your own strength & courage rather than relying on anyone

"Have you ever heard of the 'Face on Mars'? Many believe that it is proof of aliens, or at least evidence of their previous existence. But as a NASA scientist myself, I can assure you that after years of studying it, there is no evidence supporting those beliefs, and in fact, all the facts we've collected point to the 'Face on Mars' simply being a natural formation, a mere butte or mesa. 

First of all, let's start with the origins of the 'Face.' It was first discovered by NASA's Viking 1 space mission over twenty years ago. However, due to limited technological capabilities at the time of the photograph, the photo was grainy and lacked detail, which led people to believe they were looking at a man-made creation. This was fueled, in part by a number of science films and books that featured Mars as a location inhabited by otherworldly, intelligent beings, which further popularizationized the idea. This belief was then taken over to mainstream media, where they further perpetuated the idea that the Face was an alien construction, even in popular television show like the 'X Files.' However, when NASA returned to Mars in a follow-up visit, with the Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft in 1997, they photographed the Cydonia region again using much advanced technology than the one they had previously. This time the pictures came out much clearer, and it was evident that the so-called Martian "face" was not an actual face at all, and that it was just an oddly shaped mountain that had eroded and weathered in a way that created an image that resembled a man's face.

In addition to NASA's high-resolution photographs, we've collected data from laser altimetry to prove the 'Face on Mars' is indeed a natural formation. This means we've used a tool that allows us to determine the exact location, altitude and terrain of the "face." The information we've gathered shows that the 'face' is actually a type of mesas or buttes, that are also found on the planet earth. The fact that there are similar landforms, on earth, makes it clear that the face is a naturally occurring structure, which is formed by the gradual process of natural forces like the movement of tectonic plates, which can cause mountains and valleys to form over long periods.

Finally, let's talk about the location of the Cydonia region. NASA has long studied the region and it has been found out that it could be a boundary of an ancient Martian ocean. The geological evidence that we collected has shown that Mars was once much more like earth- with a warmer and more hospitable climate. This has raised the question that perhaps at a time before the Martian ocean evaporated, intelligent beings may have actually existed on Mars, but there is currently absolutely no evidence supporting that claim.

In conclusion, while it is easy for one to believe that the Face on Mars is a sign of extraterrestrial life, it is just that- a belief, and it has not been supported by any evidence, despite extensive NASA research. All evidence points to the 'Face on Mars', as a natural landform, similar to buttes on earth, and its location near a possible Martian ancient ocean. So, if you are ever asked if the 'Face on Mars', is a sign of intelligent, extraterrestrial life- remember all the facts we collected, it is indeed nothing more than a mountain. "
